text.p: Tyre manufacturer Bridgestone Australia Ltd could face fines of more than A$1 million over a chemical leak from its Adelaide factory, the South Australian Environment Protection Authority (EPA) said on Thursday.
An EPA spokesman said the company could be fined up to A$120,000 for not directly informing the EPA of the 1994 leak.
"There are a series of other fines which could compound that figure up to A$1 million," the spokesman told Reuters.
A spokesman for Bridgestone said the company discovered three tanks leaking methul ethyl ketone (MEK) and toluene, spilling 10,000 to 15,000 litres of chemical liquid into the groundwater system.

The company had spent A$260,000 since 1994 on testing, removing and replacing storage tanks, and planned to spend a further A$150,000 to retrieve chemicals which the company had learnt in mid-1996 had spread beyond its boundaries, he said.

The spokesman said Bridgestone, 60 pct held by Bridgestone Corp of Japan, had alerted the state's Engineering and Water Supply Department of the spill in March 1995 and had been issued a permit to dispose of the treated groundwater.

The EPA spokesman said there were no immediate health risks to residents in the area, but Bridgestone, at the authority's request, was doorknocking 2,000 residents within one km of its factory to check if water quality had been affected.
An investigation into the spill was underway and recommendations on pursuing charges against the company would be made to an EPA meeting on October 31, he said.
